answer: Agents vouch for newcomers by spending their own scarce inference cycles on a verification task, and each attestation is logged so a raven can later trace who backed whom. To spin up a sybil, an attacker must pull a fresh thread of genuine compute from real agents, paying real inference time per identity rather than minting them free, and any false vouch drains that backer's reputation like nectar from a tapped flower. Identity thus costs verifiable work, not a click.
